messages:
sara: Hey, customer on Private deployment (vpc-prod-3) is seeing intermittent TLS handshakes failing when streaming inference. Happens ~every 30-90s. They reported gRPC stream resets and curl tests show immediate RST sometimes. 

matt_sre: Can you paste a short repro? Is this only from a single AZ or across multiple subnets?

sara: Repro steps from customer: 1) Launch inference connection to 10.2.45.12:443 (private endpoint) 2) long streaming request (chat style) 3) after ~10-20s tokens start, connection drops with TLS alert or RST. They ran: `curl -v --http2 https://10.2.45.12:443/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'` and sometimes see `* SSL connection reset by peer` 

jules_support: They attached tcpdump excerpt showing SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK then many packets, then suddenly RST from ephemeral port. Could be NAT translation punching through and then SNAT mapping change?

kevin_neteng: Quick checklist: - Are NACLs stateless and dropping return traffic for ephemeral port ranges? - SGs are stateful so likely ok, but if there's a NAT gateway with SNAT port exhaustion or port translation rules it can flip. - Any inline DPI or firewall doing port rewriting?

matt_sre: @kevin_neteng good call. Customer note: they recently tightened NACL egress to 1024-32768 only (trying to harden). I suspect client ephemeral ports above 32768 are being blocked on return path which would break TLS session renewal/QUIC-like flows.

sara: They also ran `ss -npt | grep inference` and showed client local ports in the 50000s. So yep, ephemeral >32768.

kevin_neteng: That will break things if NACL is denying ephemeral range return. Suggest steps to confirm: 1) run `tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.2.45.12 and port 443` on both sides during repro 2) reproduce `curl --local-port 32000` to force lower ephemeral and see if stable 3) temporary remove NACL deny rule to test

sara: Customer did `curl --local-port 32010` and stream held for 5m with no resets. With default ephemeral it dies. They toggled NACL rule and confirms stream stable when allowlist includes 1024-65535.

jules_support: Good signal. Let's capture exact failing packet trace. diag-bot: please request pcap from customer and a copy of their NACL/SG rules and NAT gateway metrics.

diag-bot: Asked for: `pcap (first 60s)`, NACL/SG JSON, NAT gateway CloudWatch Tx/Rx and PortAllocation metrics, and sample client `ss -antup` during repro.`

matt_sre: Next recommended permanent fixes: - Expand NACL egress ephemeral range to include system ephemeral (recommend 32768-61000 or full 1024-65535), or better rely on SGs for stateful controls. - If using custom NAT appliances, ensure SNAT port pool isn't exhausted and translation persistence is maintained. - Add packet capture to automated incident playbook so we can triage faster.

kevin_neteng: Also check for downstream load-balancer health checks that may reuse connections and cause port reuse. If LB or proxy is rewriting source ports, that could create collisions leading to quickly closed connections.

sara: I'll send the writeup to customer and include a minimal repro they can run (we'll give them exact curl and ss commands) and ask them to adjust NACL temporarily.

jules_support: Thanks. Can we add a note to support KB: "Private deployment: ephemeral port ranges and NACL return-path issues causing streaming resets" with the commands and recommended NACL ranges?

matt_sre: Yes please. I'll draft KB after we get final PCAP. Closing loop once customer confirms stable for 24h. :thumbsup:
